control_classes.POSITIVE: A known signal expected to be recovered if the approach can detect the relevant phenomenon.
control_classes.NEGATIVE: An appropriate absence or irrelevant entity expected not to produce the claimed signal.
control_classes.NULL: A specified null process or reference distribution with explicit statistical assumptions.
control_classes.SPECIFICITY: A comparison testing whether a signal is specific to the proposed explanation.
control_classes.ROBUSTNESS: A justified perturbation testing the stability of an analytical conclusion.
control_classes.CONFOUNDER: A test of an alternative explanatory factor or design imbalance.
control_classes.FALSIFICATION: A test whose outcome could challenge a stated claim under explicit assumptions.

scientific_levels.TECHNICAL: Properties of measurement, implementation, or computational operation.
scientific_levels.STATISTICAL: Sampling, estimation, null models, or inferential assumptions.
scientific_levels.BIOLOGICAL: Empirical biological signals and context-dependent absence or specificity.
scientific_levels.MECHANISTIC: A proposed functional or causal biological mechanism.

notes: Control class and scientific level are independent axes.
A statistical null procedure is not necessarily a biological negative control.
This vocabulary has not undergone external ontology validation.
